content:
Scientific Concept: Maxwell's Equations of Electrodynamics
Domain: physics / electromagnetism
Definition: Unified set of coupled partial differential equations describing how electric and magnetic fields are generated and altered by charges and currents.

Principles:
Gauss's Law for Electricity: Electric flux through closed surface proportional to enclosed charge: div(E) = rho / epsilon_0
Gauss's Law for Magnetism: No magnetic monopoles exist: div(B) = 0
Faraday's Law of Induction: Time-varying magnetic field induces electric field: curl(E) = -dB/dt
Ampere-Maxwell Law: Magnetic fields induced by electric currents and displacement current: curl(B) = mu_0 J + mu_0 epsilon_0 dE/dt

Experimental Proofs:
Heinrich Hertz spark-gap electromagnetic wave transmission experiments (1887)
Speed of light c = 1/sqrt(mu_0 * epsilon_0) matching astronomical and laboratory optical measurements

Applications:
Wireless telecommunications
Radar
Electrical power generators
Optics
